title: Nested and Child Routes knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Nested and Child Routes”?
options: Nested and Child Routes should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Nested and Child Routes helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.

questions.answer_key: Nested and Child Routes helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Nested and Child Routes is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.answer_key: Connect “Parent and child route configuration” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Parent and child route configuration” under Nested and Child Routes. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Nested and Child Routes”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.

questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
